work.title: Work
work.lead: If you only read one entry, read the first. The rest shows how I got there.

cto.text: Overall responsibility for strategy, development, and operations of the marketplace and ERP platform. Next.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, Turborepo, Railway, Cloudflare. Commission models and payouts stay configurable, so a new market does not require a code change.

ecommerce.text: Product responsibility for the online shops: roadmap, Shopify, and the connections to warehouse and customer service.

engineer.text: An Angular 19 application in an Nx monorepo, UI from Figma with Tailwind, and interfaces over OpenAPI and RxJS.

projects.title: Projects
projects.lead: Reading about it is one thing. Here are three things you can click: the store I run today, Wire's source, and the thesis code.
projects.note: Wire fetches sources, keeps an index, and asks Jev one yes/no question. The repository is public.

wire.where: Python · Qdrant · Jev · one process, many desks
wire.text: Wire reads a set of sources on a schedule, keeps an index, and asks Jev one yes/no question about every new story. Which sources, how often, which question — that is a desk.

events.text: The backend from my thesis: an event manager with staff, lines, business units, feedback and votes. Written in 2023 entirely by prompting chat-based AI models — the experiment the thesis is about. Archived unchanged.

smartport.text: The marketplace I run as CTO: storefront, seller payouts, search, shipping and compliance on one platform. Not a demo — this is the shop that takes orders.

education.title: Education
education.lead: Two lines. The thesis is the interesting one if you work with AI in the browser.
education.text: Bachelor's examination on 19 December 2023. The thesis at Randstad Digital looks at what chat-based AI models can carry in web development, and where they stop.

offer.meta: AI consulting for small businesses in Rhine-Main | Robin Prause
offer.description: More time for your real work: I come along with small businesses in Frankfurt and Rhine-Main, find the task that eats the most time and set it up for a fixed price.
offer.service: AI and automation for small businesses
offer.message: Which tasks take up a lot of your time each week?

hero.lede: I look at how you work and set up software to reduce the work you do by hand.
hero.cta: Arrange a visit to your business
hero.hint: My time observing your work is free in the first year. I give you the setup price before the work starts.
hero.by: Robin Prause from Rodgau near Frankfurt. For small businesses, freelancers and individuals.

gain.title: What you gain
gain.text: That much time comes back from a single task that costs two hours a week today.

fast.d: Requests are sorted, quotes are prepared.

evening.d: The office stays closed at night and at the weekend.

own.d: The accounts are registered to your business. You keep access to them.

partner.d: If you like, I stay on after the handover.

top.title: Examples from everyday work
top.lead: These tasks cost a lot of time in almost every business. The easiest place to start is usually the office, with invoices and bookkeeping.

one.d: Supplier, date and amount from an emailed invoice appear in your accounts by themselves.

two.d: Every email lands in the right folder, the right person is told, and a reply is waiting as a draft.

three.d: Customers get a personal confirmation within a minute, and you get a short note.

four.d: The request turns into a draft with your prices. You check it and send it.

five.d: Friendly reminders go out on time, and paid invoices are ticked off by themselves.

six.d: Customers pick a free slot and get a reminder the day before.

seven.d: Every month all receipts are collected and handed over, with no searching.

top.more: That is only the start. The catalogue lists more than 60 further examples, sorted by area, and every offer with example prices.

about.title: About me
about.lead: With me, your business is the focus, not the technology. I listen, look at your daily work and set up exactly the task you want to get rid of.

p1.d: I have worked in software development: software, online shops, platforms.

p2.d: I have built software with AI. My bachelor thesis was already about it.

p3.d: from employers, quoted in full on this site.

p5.d: I live in Rodgau near Frankfurt and come to your business.

p6.d: at a time, so each one has my full attention.

about.who: Small businesses of up to 20 people where the owner decides, for example landscaping, waste disposal, farming and service businesses. Also freelancers, the self-employed and individuals.

ai.q: Do we need to know about AI?
ai.a: You know your work, and that is enough. I take care of the technology and practise with you until you can do the task on your own.

cost.a: My time observing your work is free in the first year. Afterwards I name the task and a fixed sum before the work starts. Example prices are in the offer catalogue.

start.q: Where is the best place to start?
start.a: Usually the office: invoices, emails and quotes. That is where most of the time goes in almost every business. We set up one task properly, and once it runs, the next one follows.

auto.q: Does everything run fully automatically then?
auto.a: Routine work does. You decide on anything important: quotes, replies to complaints and payments arrive as drafts, and you approve them with one click.

own.q: Who owns the accounts and the data?
own.a: You do. All accounts are in your name, and you pay for the tools directly to the provider. With a custom build, the code is yours as well.

privacy.a: I use company accounts with a data processing agreement and privacy-friendly settings. We decide together which data goes into the tool. A person checks every result before it goes out.

act.q: What is the EU AI Act about?
act.a: Since February 2025 every company that uses AI tools at work has to make sure its people are AI literate. That applies to small businesses too. The training “AI literacy for the team” covers it, with a certificate of attendance.

time.q: How much of our time does this take?
time.a: During my visit, you simply carry on as usual. For practising you plan a few short sessions. After that you save time.

after.a: You get instructions for everyday use and simple changes. If you need help with technical problems, ongoing support is available.

extra.q: Are there costs on top of the prices?
extra.a: You pay for the tools themselves monthly, directly to the provider. I tell you these costs before we start.

end.title: Fancy more free time?
end.text: Tell me in two or three sentences what piles up for you. I reply personally, and we arrange a visit.

foot.note: Example calculation: two hours a week over 50 working weeks. How much time you actually gain depends on your business and the task. The workflows and figures on this page are examples, and the prices in the catalogue are guide values. The offer you receive after I have come along is the binding one.

privacy.description: What happens to personal data on this site.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: What happens to personal data on this site. If the English and German texts ever differ, the German text applies.
privacy.host: The site is hosted by Render Services, Inc., United States, on a server in Frankfurt am Main. Render processes data so the site can be delivered. Because Render is based in the United States, access from there can happen. That rests on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework or, where that does not apply, on the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.
privacy.logs: When a page is opened, the server processes the IP address, date and time, the address requested, the browser identifier, and the status of the response. This is needed to deliver the page and to keep the service secure. It is not used for advertising, and it is not built into a profile. The legal basis is Article 6 (1) (f) GDPR: a working and secure site. The host keeps these logs for its operational period. This site does not keep a log archive of its own.
privacy.storageTitle: Cookies and storage on your device
privacy.storage: This site sets no cookies. There is no analytics and no advertising. Fonts are loaded from this site, not from another provider. If you choose Light or Dark, that choice is stored on your device under the name prause-theme. The legal basis is section 25 (2) TDDDG: the storage exists for a setting you switch on yourself.
privacy.mail: The form sends your name, email address, and message to mail@robin-prause.de. This site does not store the message. It passes through the Render server in Frankfurt to the Hostinger mailbox, where it stays until I delete it. The basis is Article 6 (1) (b) GDPR when you ask about working together, otherwise Article 6 (1) (f) GDPR so I can answer. The mail link next to the form still opens your own mail program.
privacy.rights: You can ask for access, correction, deletion and restriction, and you can object to processing that rests on legitimate interest. You can also lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.
privacy.authority: The Hessian Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information, Gustav-Stresemann-Ring 1, 65189 Wiesbaden.
